newsitem.title: MACEDONIA: Macedonia holds second round in local polls.
newsitem.headline: Macedonia holds second round in local polls.

text.p: Voters went to the polls on Sunday in the second round of Macedonia's hotly-contested local elections which the ruling SDAM party and opposition say are a trial run for national elections.
The ruling party, led by Prime Minister Branko Crvenkovski, and the opposition coalition were vying for 81 municipalities including the capital Skopje.

The opposition, which has criticised the government's rapid free-market reforms as "corrupt", hoped to make a strong showing in the election, the first local poll since Macedonia gained independence in 1991 from the old Yugoslavia.
Only 33 out of 124 municipalities had mayors elected in the first round held on November 17. Official results of the local elections are expected within three days.
Observers from the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) and other international bodies reported some irregularities in the first round, citing incomplete electoral lists.

But the head of the OSCE mission in Skopje, Christian Faber Rot, told reporters there were no plans for monitoring the second round because "there were no larger or significant faults in the process".
